Q: Running junit parameterized tests (not classes) in parallel A:

JUnit 5 has built-in support for running tests in parallel. The official documentation is undoubtedly the best source to check it out: https://junit.org/junit5/docs/snapshot/user-guide/#writing-tests-parallel-execution

Q: Applying FUN in ave() to only a subset of the group A:

a {data.table} solution:

library(data.table)

as.data.table(x)[, B := mean(B[C < 3]), by = A][, B]

output:

[1] 1.5 1.5 3.5 3.5 3.5

Q: Running sh or bash script commands from the bottom to the top A:

If you have a list of commands that you sometimes want to run in one direction and sometimes the reverse, consider writing your script to take an argument dictating the order of execution, e.g.:

$ cat tst.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash

cmdA() { echo 'ran cmdA'; }
cmdB() { echo 'ran cmdB'; }
cmdC() { echo 'ran cmdC'; }

cmds=( cmdA cmdB cmdC )
min=0
max="${#cmds[@]}"

if [[ $1 == "b" ]]; then
    beg="$(( max - 1 ))"
    end="$(( min - 1 ))"
    chg='-1'
else
    beg="$min"
    end="$max"
    chg='1'
fi

for (( i="$beg"; i!="$end"; i+="$chg" )); do
    "${cmds[i]}"
done


$ ./tst.sh
ran cmdA
ran cmdB
ran cmdC


$ ./tst.sh b
ran cmdC
ran cmdB
ran cmdA

Q: How to merge N DataFrames into one, while using first DF as reference? A:

concat() isn't working for you because you picked the wrong axis. You also didn't set the index for it to join on. (Note: It doesn't have a way to select an on column, unlike merge().)

By the way, instead of looping, pass all the dfs at once.

Here I'm also reindexing ahead of time so that I can supply a fill_value to avoid conversion to float.

pd.concat(
    [d.set_index('Object').reindex(object_list, fill_value=0) for d in dfs],
    axis=1)

   Dataset A  Dataset B  Dataset C
A       1000       1000          0
B         50          0          0
C          1         30       2000
D          0          0        100

Setup:

object_list = pd.Series(['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'])
dfs = [
    pd.DataFrame({'Object': ['A', 'B', 'C'], 'Dataset A': [1000, 50, 1]}),
    pd.DataFrame({'Object': ['A', 'C'], 'Dataset B': [1000, 30]}),
    pd.DataFrame({'Object': ['C', 'D'], 'Dataset C': [2000, 100]})]

I know you said object_list is a DataFrame, but based on your description, it should really be a Series, so I changed it here because it makes the example code simpler. To convert to series, you could select out the Object column or use .squeeze(axis=1).
